Ascent.name: Ascent
Ascent.summary: Ascent has two bombsites, A and B, joined by a central mid area that acts as the main rotation hub. Attackers enter each site through a narrow main lane (A Main or B Main), while manually operated doors can block sightlines during plants and retakes.

A Site: Clear Heaven and Hell before planting, since both give defenders hidden angles on the bomb.
Push A Main as the main entry and smoke off Wine or the Tree route to cut off flanks.
Retake through A Lobby with a flash, and check Heaven (A Rafters) and Hell last.
Spot Window and Garden with a player or utility before committing, since they can open flank sightlines.
B Site: Stun the B Lobby corner before entering B Main so the lane is not shot at as you go in.
Hold Boat House from the back corner; it covers both the plant spot and the approach from the lobby.
When retaking, commit to one side of the bombsite, since Boat House and B Main cover different angles.
Mid: Take Mid Top and Catwalk early to control the A rotation, or you will get pinched mid-push.
Hold Mid Cubby from the flank to pick off players moving up toward Catwalk.
Move through Mid Market quickly as a B rotation path before the defenders can smoke it.
Keep Courtyard and Mid Link open as rotation routes so a mid split does not cut off one site.

callouts.name: A Door
callouts.description: The closable metal door between Tree and A Site; shut it to cut the route from mid onto A.

callouts.name: A Garden
callouts.description: The defender-side room just west of A Site, joining the site to Window and Tree and covering the Tree exit.

callouts.name: A Generator
callouts.description: The tall generator box on A Site, the main cover for the plant and a common spot to hold A Main from.

callouts.name: A Link
callouts.description: The route from the top of Mid Catwalk into Tree, how a mid split reaches A Site.

callouts.name: A Lobby
callouts.description: The open area that feeds straight into A Main, so it is the usual staging point before an A push.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.description: The narrow main lane into A Site, where most early A fights happen and where attackers usually push first.

callouts.name: A Rafters
callouts.description: The raised walkway over the back of A Site, called Heaven by most players; it watches the whole site and the A Main entrance.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The A bombsite itself, where defenders hold and attackers plant.

callouts.name: A Tree
callouts.description: The small room between A Main and Mid Catwalk, the link attackers use to join a mid player onto A.

callouts.name: A Window
callouts.description: The window on the defender side of A that looks across Garden; defenders peek it to catch Tree and Catwalk pushes.

callouts.name: A Wine
callouts.description: The corner at the far end of A Main by the site entrance, a common close-range hiding spot.

callouts.name: Hell
callouts.description: The low spot under Heaven at the back of A Site, a hidden angle for a defender or a post-plant hide.

callouts.name: B Back
callouts.description: The back corner of B Site toward Boat House, a deep spot to hold the site from or to play a retake out of.

callouts.name: B Boat House
callouts.description: The side room off the back of B Site; defenders hold it to cover the plant and attackers clear it first.

callouts.name: B Default
callouts.description: The stacked boxes in the middle of B Site where the spike is usually planted.

callouts.name: B Door
callouts.description: The closable door between Market and B Site, the defenders' rotation door from mid; shut it to stop the Market push.

callouts.name: B Lobby
callouts.description: The area that leads into B Main, where attackers usually stun or flash the lane before pushing in.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.description: The main entry lane into B Site, and a common sniper position for early duels.

callouts.name: B Pillar
callouts.description: The pillar on the Market side of B Site, cover for a defender and a spot attackers clear before planting.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The B bombsite, a box-filled area that gives cover for planting and holding.

callouts.name: Mid Bottom
callouts.description: The defender end of mid between Courtyard and Market, where mid control is won or lost.

callouts.name: Mid Catwalk
callouts.description: The elevated path running from mid up toward A Link and A Site, often peeked from the side.

callouts.name: Mid Courtyard
callouts.description: The open central area of mid, where many mid fights start and rotations pass through.

callouts.name: Mid Cubby
callouts.description: A small nook at the top of Catwalk on the A side, a hiding spot for picks on players heading to A Link.

callouts.name: Mid Link
callouts.description: The short connector between Mid Courtyard and B Main, used to rotate or to hit B Main from the side.

callouts.name: Mid Market
callouts.description: The defender-side building between mid and B Site, the main rotation path from mid to B.

callouts.name: Mid Pizza
callouts.description: The small room between Market and the defender side, a rotation spot for defenders moving through mid.

callouts.name: Mid Top
callouts.description: The attacker end of mid, by the top of Catwalk, where attackers gather before taking mid.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: Where the attacking team starts each round.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: Where the defending team starts each round.

Bind.name: Bind
Bind.summary: Bind is a two-site map with no middle lane. Two one-way teleporters take the place of a mid, letting teams move between A and B quickly, and each one is loud enough that using it gives the opposing team a sound cue. Most fights happen at the A and B entrances, so the callouts cluster around the Lamps, Bath, Hookah and Garden areas.

A Site: A Tower sits on high ground that only defenders can reach and watches the Bath and A Short from above, so flash or smoke A Lamps before walking under it.
The A Bath holds an Ult Orb, so contest it when your team is ult-heavy and cover the longer route from A Short while you do.
The A Teleporter is loud when someone uses it, so listen for it to learn when enemies are rotating, and use the sound as a fake when you need to pull attention away from the real push.
B Site: B Garden and B Long are separated by a metal tube and B Long is often smoked, so only commit to the B Long push when you have information from the teleporter side.
The B Window (Hookah) is the usual entry point, so place utility there to cover the B Short and B Garden approaches before you peek.
The B Cubby sits right under the Hookah, so a defender holding it can be cleared with a flash or thrown utility from the window.

callouts.name: A Bath
callouts.description: A tiled bathroom on the A side that opens directly onto A Site.

callouts.name: A Cubby
callouts.description: A small alcove on the back side of A Site where a defender can hold a corner.

callouts.name: A Exit
callouts.description: An exit area on the A side where a teleporter drops players off.

callouts.name: A Lamps
callouts.description: A tight, cornered room near the A Teleporter and A Short, with high ground above it. Defenders often hide inside.

callouts.name: A Link
callouts.description: A Link is the rotation route that leads into A Short.

callouts.name: A Lobby
callouts.description: A Lobby is the exit of the B Long teleporter, located next to A Bath.

callouts.name: A Short
callouts.description: A narrow passage that leads to the front of A Site, sitting close to A Lamps and the A Teleporter.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The A bombsite, which holds the stacked crates, the Truck, and the high ground of A Tower.

callouts.name: A Teleporter
callouts.description: A Teleporter is the teleporter on the A Short side that sends players to B Short or B Hookah.

callouts.name: A Tower
callouts.description: Elevated high ground above A Lamps that overlooks A Short and the Bath approach. Only defenders can reach it.

callouts.name: A Truck
callouts.description: The truck parked on A Site, the big piece of cover in the middle of the site.

callouts.name: B Cubby
callouts.description: The corner on B Site right under Hookah's window, a close hiding spot attackers check as they walk onto the site.

callouts.name: B Elbow
callouts.description: A curved corridor behind B Site that joins the defender spawn.

callouts.name: B Exit
callouts.description: An exit area on the B side where a teleporter drops players off.

callouts.name: B Fountain
callouts.description: B Fountain is the fountain area outside B Long, which connects to the attacker spawn.

callouts.name: B Garden
callouts.description: An outdoor area just before B Hookah and B Long, separated from B Long by a metal tube.

callouts.name: B Hall
callouts.description: A passage visible from the B Cubby that leads toward the B site.

callouts.name: B Link
callouts.description: The marketplace connector on the B side, which forms the link between the B side and the A side together with A Link.

callouts.name: B Long
callouts.description: A long corridor that leads to B Site, next to B Garden and the B Teleporter. It is often smoked or walled off.

callouts.name: B Short
callouts.description: A passage on the B side that connects to the hookah area and the arrival point of the A teleporter.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The B bombsite, with crates and the Cubby on one side and the Hookah window above the entry.

callouts.name: B Teleporter
callouts.description: B Teleporter is the B Long-side teleporter that drops players into A Lobby next to A Bath (Showers).

callouts.name: B Window
callouts.description: A window-style overlook on the B side that looks down into B Site, sitting beside the B Short exit.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Cave
callouts.description: A cave-like area on the attacker side that defenders can use to flank.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The attacking team's starting area at the far end of the map, where attackers begin each round and regroup before a push.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defenders' starting area, reached from the B side through the B Elbow corridor.

Haven.name: Haven
Haven.summary: Haven is the original three-site map: A on the east, B in the middle and C on the west. Attackers hit A through A Long or Sewer, B straight through Mid, and C through C Long or Garage. With three sites to cover, defenders rely on fast rotations through A Link and C Link behind each site.

A Site: Hit A Long and Short at the same time; one defender can't hold both.
Clear A Tower and A Hell before planting, as both see the default spot.
Defenders: a single smoke on A Long buys time for the A Link rotation.
B Site: B falls fast to a Mid Courtyard push, so defenders should play it from a distance and rely on rotations.
After planting on B, play the A Link and C Link exits; that is where the retake comes from.
Check B Back on entry, it is a common spot for a lurking defender.
C Site: Fake C Long and send the real push through Garage to catch C defenders facing the wrong way.
Clear C Cubby and Logs on the way in; both are easy to walk past.
C Platform sees all of Long, so smoke or flash it before the lane push.
Mid: Mid Courtyard is the fastest way to B, so whoever owns it controls the pace of the round.
Mid Doors lets you swing from mid onto C through Garage without using Long.
Don't stand in the open courtyard; it can be shot from Window and both links.

callouts.name: A Box
callouts.description: The boxes on A Site at the A Short entrance, cover for a defender while a teammate holds Tower.

callouts.name: A Garden
callouts.description: The attacker-side area behind A Lobby, where attackers group before splitting into Long or Sewer.

callouts.name: A Graffiti
callouts.description: The painted wall on the A Link side of A Site, where defenders sit to catch attackers coming onto site.

callouts.name: A Heaven Stairs
callouts.description: The stairs up to A Tower (Heaven) at the back of A Site, the defenders' way up to the high ground.

callouts.name: A Hell
callouts.description: The low corner tucked under A Tower, a hidden angle on anyone planting.

callouts.name: A Link
callouts.description: The defender-side corridor between A Site and B, the main rotation between those two sites.

callouts.name: A Lobby
callouts.description: The attacker-side area in front of A Long and Sewer, where A pushes are set up.

callouts.name: A Long
callouts.description: The long approach that leads straight into A Site, where defenders often hold angles down the lane.

callouts.name: A Ramp
callouts.description: The slope where A Long comes up onto A Site; Tower overlooks it, so attackers clear it before stepping on site.

callouts.name: A Sewer
callouts.description: The tunnel off A Lobby that comes up into A Short, the attackers' second way onto A Site.

callouts.name: A Short
callouts.description: The short route from Sewer onto A Site; hitting Short and A Long together splits the defenders.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The first bomb site on the east side, where most A plants and retakes happen.

callouts.name: A Tower
callouts.description: The raised ledge over the back of A Site, watching A Long and the site from above.

callouts.name: B Back
callouts.description: The back of B Site toward defender spawn, a deep spot to play retakes from.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The middle site, entered straight from Mid Courtyard; quick to hit, and defenders reach it from A Link and C Link.

callouts.name: C Connector
callouts.description: The short passage from Garage onto C Site, watched from Platform and Logs.

callouts.name: C Cubby
callouts.description: A small nook along C Long where a defender can hide to catch attackers pushing the lane.

callouts.name: C Garage
callouts.description: The building between mid and C Site; attackers use it to hit C from the side instead of through Long.

callouts.name: C Link
callouts.description: The defender-side corridor joining C Site to B, the main rotation between those two sites.

callouts.name: C Lobby
callouts.description: The attacker-side area that feeds both C Long and Garage.

callouts.name: C Logs
callouts.description: The stacked logs on the B side of C Site, a close hiding spot covering the Garage exit.

callouts.name: C Long
callouts.description: The long lane that leads from the attacker side into C Site, where most C pushes are fought.

callouts.name: C Platform
callouts.description: The raised ledge at the far back of C Site, a deep angle over C Long and the plant.

callouts.name: C Site
callouts.description: The third bomb site on the west side, reached through the long lane and a garage area.

callouts.name: C Window
callouts.description: The window between C Link and Garage; defenders peek it to catch attackers coming out of Garage.

callouts.name: Mid Courtyard
callouts.description: The central open space that connects to all three sites and is where rotations usually cross.

callouts.name: Mid Doors
callouts.description: The doorway on the C side of mid into Garage, a fast route from mid to C.

callouts.name: Mid Window
callouts.description: The window into Mid Courtyard; whoever holds it sees players crossing mid toward B.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The attacking team's starting area where early utility and rotations begin.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defending team's starting area, from which defenders set up and rotate to sites.

Fracture.name: Fracture
Fracture.summary: Fracture is an H-shaped map with A on one wing and B on the other, joined by a single central Defender Side Spawn and no traditional mid lane. Attackers start from spawns at both ends of the H and cross the map on one-way ziplines, so defenders have to watch two approach directions at once.

A Site: Put one player on A Rope to hear pushes through the A Hall door and a second on A Dish to catch lurkers coming from the satellite area.
When you lose A Main or A Hall, fall back toward the Defender Side Spawn and retake with the team, because attackers have several entries and holding alone is costly.
As an attacker, use the plant behind the box on the lower level, which was the most popular plant spot in playtest, and avoid A Drop unless you can cover the noise of the drop.
B Site: Take B Tower early with a teammate, since it covers Arcade, the Tunnel, and the B Main push, and crossfire it because parts of the walls can be shot through.
As an attacker, clear B Tower first, then pincer the site from the Tunnel while the rest of the team pushes B Main.
Check the alcove next to the site and the central boxes before calling a clean site, since both are common plant spots.
Mid: Use the Defender Side Spawn as the fastest connector, but do not hold it alone with attacker utility still in hand, because attackers can trap defenders in the middle third.
Attackers who ride the long ziplines silently are slower, but the silence masks their sound from defenders in the Defender Side Spawn.

callouts.name: A Dish
callouts.description: The satellite-dish area on the A side, where a lurker can cover an attacker push or a rotation, so defenders often keep someone watching it.

callouts.name: A Door
callouts.description: The door set inside the A Hall corridor that opens toward A Rope and the Defender Side Spawn, which is why defenders listen there when a push comes through the hall.

callouts.name: A Drop
callouts.description: A northern entry into A Site from the raised box area, where a defender can jump down while an attacker dropping in makes enough noise to be heard.

callouts.name: A Gate
callouts.description: Spot on the outer side of the Attacker Side Spawn, away from the map centre, where a security-card interactive sits on a rock next to it.

callouts.name: A Hall
callouts.description: The main entrance corridor into A Site, placed ahead of A Door and A Main, and the spot defenders call when they hear a push coming through the hallway.

callouts.name: A Link
callouts.description: A southern entry into A Site, one of the routes that feeds attackers in from the bottom of the map alongside A Main and A Rope.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.description: The attacker route onto A Site that runs beside A Hall, usually regarded as the strongest defensive angle on A, and the call for a push on the front of the site.

callouts.name: A Rope
callouts.description: The area beside the A Hall door where a defender can listen to pushes, and the path attackers use to reach the Defender Side Spawn.

callouts.name: A Sand
callouts.description: The sandy area between A Rope and A Main, the open space attackers cross on their way onto A.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The plant zone on the left wing of the map that every A-side route feeds into, and the reference point for calls such as A Hall, A Main, and A Link.

callouts.name: B Arcade
callouts.description: The arcade building on the B side between B Tower and B Bench, a route onto B from the top half of the attacker spawn.

callouts.name: B Bench
callouts.description: Lane area on the B side, reached from Attacker Side Bridge.

callouts.name: B Canteen
callouts.description: The canteen beside B Generator on the B side, a hold spot covering pushes out of B Tunnel.

callouts.name: B Generator
callouts.description: A tall cover spot on the B side near the site, valued because it gives a defender cover and a comfortable hold next to the B Canteen.

callouts.name: B Link
callouts.description: The northern entry into B Site, mirroring the southern B Main approach, and a route defenders watch when rotating from the middle of the map.

callouts.name: B Lobby
callouts.description: The attacker area at the top of the map that feeds B Bench and B Arcade, where B pushes from that half of spawn are set up.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.description: The attacker push route into B Site from the south, which defenders usually watch from B Tower.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The plant zone on the right wing of the map, with many angles and hiding spots, where attackers arrive through several entrances.

callouts.name: B Tower
callouts.description: An elevated defensive position on B Site that watches Arcade, the Tunnel, and the B Main push, and that defenders are advised to hold in a crossfire because some of its walls can be shot through.

callouts.name: B Tree
callouts.description: A spot in the greener Alpha sector just past the main entrance and before the B Site.

callouts.name: B Tunnel
callouts.description: The underpass beneath the B side that attackers use to rotate around B Site, watched from B Tower, and one of the few map features that stayed unchanged from the earliest prototype.

callouts.name: Zipline
callouts.description: The one-way ziplines under Defender Spawn that carry attackers between the two halves of their spawn.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Bridge
callouts.description: Attacker-side bridge that leads from Attacker Side Spawn into the B Bench ramp, so it is the attacker route toward B rather than a bridge over the map centre.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: One of the two attacker spawns, placed at opposite ends of the H-shaped map, from which attackers ride a one-way zipline to the far end, which is why the spawn split matters for defense.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The central defender spawn in the middle of the H, above the zipline, and the only efficient connector between the A and B sites, which makes it the main rotation point.

Split.name: Split
Split.summary: Split is a two-site map with the A and B bombsites at opposite ends and a narrow central Mid linking them through vents, sewer and rope passages. Mid is the hub that nearly every round is fought over, and the Heaven spots above each site overlook the approaches. Expect the A side to play through Main, Ramps and Screens, and the B side to funnel through a narrow Hallway into a pillar-heavy site.

A Site: Take A Main and the Ramps before pushing the site. Holding the top of Ramps gives a wide view, but it is usually the first place defenders check on a retake.
After taking A, clear A Tower (Heaven). A vent drops from there into Mid, so defenders can use it to rotate.
On defense, put one player on Screens for information and one at the top of Ramps who falls back to Rafters when pushed. Watch for pushes coming up from Mid.
B Site: The B Hallway is narrow and the corners are sharp. Clear each corner methodically, and check the back corners near Double Box with a flash or recon before advancing.
Use the pillar to stall one-on-one fights. Attackers need to wrap it to clear angles.

On defense, keep the strongest defender on site and let a teammate rotate in from Mail when Mid is quiet. Stall and wait for backup rather than taking a one-versus-many fight, since B pushes often end that way.
Mid: Mid is contested almost every round and controls access to both sites, so it is worth gaining early info before committing.
On defense, watch Mid from Mail and Vent with two players, and listen for pushers using Ropes and Link.
Mid can be reached from both heavens (the A vent and the B stairs), so an enemy appearing in Mid may be rotating. Check corners before committing to a fight there.

callouts.name: A Back
callouts.description: The far corner of A Site, behind the plant spots and away from the Ramps approach, from which a player can hit a plant from the rear.

callouts.name: A Cafe
callouts.description: The room at the attacker end of A Main beside A Lobby, where A pushes gather before going up Main.

callouts.name: A Elbow
callouts.description: The bend between A Screens and A Back on the defender side of A, a close angle onto anyone walking up to the site.

callouts.name: A Lobby
callouts.description: Sits above the A Sewer and is reached from there by an ascender, so the call means someone is coming up out of the sewer toward the A side.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.description: The main lane leading from the A side toward A Site, where early contact usually happens. A player on Screens can watch the A Main crossing from behind the site.

callouts.name: A Rafters
callouts.description: A fallback spot beside A Tower, used by a defender who has been pushed off Ramps.

callouts.name: A Ramps
callouts.description: The ramp that climbs from A Main onto A Site and is the main entry point. Calling it tells the team who is holding the top of the ramp and who is pushing up it.

callouts.name: A Screens
callouts.description: A spot behind A Site with a view of the A Main crossing.

callouts.name: A Sewer
callouts.description: A passage on the A side that links toward Mid and, through an ascender, up to A Lobby. Calling it warns that enemies may come through the sewer into Mid or onto the A side.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The A bombsite, at the opposite end of the map from B Site and reached through A Main and the A Ramps. Teams use it to report plants and enemies on the site.

callouts.name: A Tower
callouts.description: The high ground above A Site that overlooks Ramps.

callouts.name: B Alley
callouts.description: The corridor on the defender side above B Site, joining B Back to the rotation route toward defender spawn.

callouts.name: B Back
callouts.description: The rear of B Site, behind the pillar and close to Default, where an attacker can plant or clear from the back.

callouts.name: B Garage
callouts.description: A front-view position on B Site and a route that attackers use to push toward the site and into Mid. Calling Garage tells the team that the B push is coming through it.

callouts.name: B Hell
callouts.description: The low corner on B Site under B Tower (Heaven), a hidden spot to hold the site from below.

callouts.name: B Link
callouts.description: A passage that runs from Mid toward the B side, one of the central passages alongside Ropes, Mail and Sewer. Calls mention it to report enemies sneaking from Mid into the B side.

callouts.name: B Lobby
callouts.description: The staging area that feeds into B Main, close to a set of boxes that players often lose to corner peeks. Calling it signals enemies gathering before they move down B Main.

callouts.name: B New Box
callouts.description: The box on the front edge of B Site, cover for a planter and a close angle on B Main.

callouts.name: B Rafters
callouts.description: A high position that defenders push onto from B Main to support a teammate fighting in that lane.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The B bombsite, reached through B Main and the B Hallway, with the pillar in the middle and Backsite behind it. Teams use it to report plants and enemy positions on the site.

callouts.name: B Stairs
callouts.description: A stairway that links the B high ground (Heaven) down toward Mid. Calling it warns of enemies moving up or down between the B high ground and Mid.

callouts.name: B Tower
callouts.description: The elevated spot on the B side above B Site.

callouts.name: Mid Bottom
callouts.description: The attacker end of mid, where attackers come in before splitting toward B Link or the A Sewer.

callouts.name: Mid Mail
callouts.description: Mid Mail is the Mid passage on the route toward Ropes; it is not a B Site callout.

callouts.name: Mid Top
callouts.description: The defender end of mid by Mail and Vent; holding it controls both mid routes.

callouts.name: Mid Vent
callouts.description: The vent that drops from the A heaven spot into Mid, so enemies can come down from above. Players often lurk near Mail and Ropes and call this vent when something drops in.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The area where the attacking team begins each round. Both the A and B routes and Mid can be reached from it, so the call tells the team where enemies are coming back from.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defending team's starting area on the B side, where each defender begins the round.

Sunset.name: Sunset
Sunset.summary: Sunset has two bombsites: a small A Site reached through A Elbow and A Link, and a larger B Site reached through B Boba and B Market. Mid Courtyard is the hub that connects both sides, with Mid Top, Mid Tiles and Mid Bottom branching off it, and the defender spawn area feeds into the upper routes at Mid Top, A Link, A Alley and B Boba.

A Site: Take A Elbow early, since holding it makes it much easier to keep the spike covered.
A Site sits far from Mid Courtyard, so defenders struggle to rotate there after a plant; time your pushes around that gap.
Clear A Alley and A Lobby with flashes before peeking, because its deep corners punish a blind entry.
B Site: Take B Main before the plant; it is the area that protects the spike, so cover late flanks there with utility.
Check the state of the B Market door before committing, because it can block sightlines and change how retakes go.
Use B Boba as the entry from Mid and A, and expect defenders to hold the site from it.
Mid: Mid Courtyard is the hub, so expect early clashes there; smoke it before moving through rather than walking into the open.
Mid Top is the defender's route to stop attackers taking Mid Courtyard, so check it when you need to cut off rotations.
Mid Tiles is a choke point; use explosive utility to hold it and watch the approach to Mid Courtyard.

callouts.name: A Alley
callouts.description: A back passage on the A side full of deep corners and tight 90-degree turns, so defenders can hold A from here and attackers need utility to clear it. It connects toward the upper defender spawn area.

callouts.name: A Elbow
callouts.description: A bend on the approach to A Site, reached from Mid along a connector route; attackers usually take it early because it makes holding the spike easier.

callouts.name: A Link
callouts.description: The connector between Mid (through Mid Top) and the upper defender spawn area on the A side; smokes placed here can block sightlines along the route.

callouts.name: A Lobby
callouts.description: The exit from the attacker spawn that leads into A Main; it works as a choke point close to Mid Tiles and A Elbow.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.description: The open fighting ground that sits just past A Lobby, where most of the A-side action takes place.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The smaller of the two bombsites, which the A Elbow, A Link and A Alley routes all feed into.

callouts.name: B Boba
callouts.description: The route linking B Site to Mid and A; attackers push B through it, and defenders can hold the site from it.

callouts.name: B Door
callouts.description: The mechanical door between Mid Courtyard and B Market; closing it cuts the mid route into B.

callouts.name: B Lobby
callouts.description: The exit from the attacker spawn that leads into B Main.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.description: The key area on the B side that attackers must take to protect the spike; late flanks through here are usually covered with utility.

callouts.name: B Market
callouts.description: The connector between B Site and Mid Courtyard, with a mechanical door between it and the courtyard.

callouts.name: B Pillar
callouts.description: The block in the middle of B Site that the site wraps around; it splits the site and blocks the view from B Main.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The larger bombsite, where the spike can only be planted in one specific area.

callouts.name: Mid Bottom
callouts.description: The lower part of the mid area, reached through Mid Courtyard.

callouts.name: Mid Box
callouts.description: The box in the middle of Mid Courtyard, the only cover for players crossing mid.

callouts.name: Mid Courtyard
callouts.description: The central hub that connects both bombsites, Mid Tiles, B Market and the upper and lower parts of mid; teams often clash here early in the round.

callouts.name: Mid Tiles
callouts.description: A section of mid that connects to Mid Courtyard and works as a choke point for holding mid.

callouts.name: Mid Top
callouts.description: The upper mid route that connects to the defender spawn area; defenders use it to stop attackers from taking Mid Courtyard.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The attackers' starting area; the lobbies leading into A and B both begin here.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defenders' starting area, which links into the upper routes including Mid Top, A Link, A Alley and B Boba.

Icebox.name: Icebox
Icebox.summary: Icebox is built around two bombsites on opposite ends of a shared central lane. A Site is reached up a conveyor-style belt and is ringed by raised nests, a rafter area and screened walkways that reward elevated positions, while B Site has a crowded front entrance and a quieter backside with a snowman structure and a tube route. Mid sits between them, with a boiler wall and pallet area, and both sites are visible from it, which makes mid the main rotation hub.

A Site: Hold A Belt or A Rafters early, because from there you can see most of the bombsite and call out pushes before they reach the plant.
Rotate through mid into the A screens to skip most of the A elevations, and use that route when the belt and nest are locked down.
Watch for zipline rushes at A Zip and nest pushes at A Nest, and use a utility or a cover player to slow them down before they reach the plant zone.
B Site: Control B Kitchen whenever possible, since it covers both mid approaches and gives clean access to the bombsite, and the defense loses most of its options without it.
Expect attackers to force the B Tube route into the kitchen, and when it happens, play for cover-heavy trades rather than a long duel in the open.
Plant spots like B Default can be targeted from B Back and B Orange, so attackers should set up bounce lineups from those angles and defenders should watch both spots.
Mid: Use Mid Blue as the anchor for lurks and push info, because it is where most mid pushes come through and it can be scanned to both sites.
Line up your angles with Mid Boiler, since both sites are visible from under the tunnel and the boiler, so holding it gives you early warning for either site.
Use smokes to block the mid tunnel and the boiler sightlines when you want to rotate safely, and avoid standing still at Mid Pallet for long because it is a common rotation path.

callouts.name: A 4-10
callouts.description: The box stack in the middle of A Site in front of the plant, cover for a planter and a common hold.

callouts.name: A Belt
callouts.description: The conveyor belt that climbs up onto A Site from the attacker side, and an elevated walkway above the site.

callouts.name: A Generator
callouts.description: The generator at the back of A Site, cover for a defender holding the site from deep.

callouts.name: A Jail
callouts.description: The fenced room beside A Nest on the attacker side of A, a hiding spot to clear before going up to the site.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.description: The attackers' main lane onto A, between Mid Blue and A Belt.

callouts.name: A Nest
callouts.description: A raised structure on A with cylindrical containers out front, visible through an opening from A Belt. It is reached by rope, zipline or ascender, and it is a plant position, so callouts here warn the team of a nest push or a plant.

callouts.name: A Pipes
callouts.description: The pipes under A Nest on the attacker approach to A, a close angle on anyone walking onto the site.

callouts.name: A Rafters
callouts.description: An elevated area over A Site that attackers and defenders both use for high-ground peeks.

callouts.name: A Screen
callouts.description: The screened walkways on A that players reach by rotating through mid, which lets them skip most of the A elevations.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The A bombsite itself, the plant zone that the attackers push into from the belt and the entry lanes.

callouts.name: A Zipline
callouts.description: The zipline across A Site between A Nest and the site, used to cross or to peek from above.

callouts.name: B Back
callouts.description: The back corner of B Site, tucked between the tunnel and the ice wall at the far side of the bombsite.

callouts.name: B Cubby
callouts.description: A cubby inside the B bombsite that sits in the front-entrance area, close to B Green and B Yellow.

callouts.name: B Fence
callouts.description: The fence on the defender side of B between B Back and B Hall, an angle over the back of the site.

callouts.name: B Garage
callouts.description: A corner inside B Site between a yellow box and a wall, which can be scanned from Mid Blue and from B Yellow.

callouts.name: B Green
callouts.description: The green containers and boxes on the B front entrance, close to B Cubby and B Yellow.

callouts.name: B Hall
callouts.description: The short hallway from B Site toward B Orange, the inside route between the site and mid.

callouts.name: B Hut
callouts.description: A hut in B Site close to the defender spawn, with a bridge above it.

callouts.name: B Kitchen
callouts.description: The kitchen area of B that gives defenders several angles on both mid approaches and clean access to the site.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.description: The attackers' main lane onto B, between B Green and B Yellow.

callouts.name: B Orange
callouts.description: An orange container on the B backside, next to a green box, from which players shoot across the site.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The B bombsite itself, which has a separate outer section at the corner by the yellow crate and the ramp.

callouts.name: B Snow Pile
callouts.description: The snow pile by B Orange on the route from mid toward Kitchen, cover for players crossing to B.

callouts.name: B Snowman
callouts.description: A snowman structure on the B backside that defenders can stand on top of to scan into A Site. It is also a defensive spot for contesting attackers who enter the open ground of B.

callouts.name: B Tube
callouts.description: A tube with an entrance on B Site that forms a hard attacking route up into the kitchen. Once attackers get through it they gain heavy cover over the B bombsite.

callouts.name: B Yellow
callouts.description: A yellow spot on the B front entrance that can be scanned from the ramp corner of the attacker spawn and from B Garage.

callouts.name: Mid Blue
callouts.description: A spot in mid where enemies push up from mid and attacker spawn, and where arrows are aimed from.

callouts.name: Mid Boiler
callouts.description: A boiler wall in mid that players walk up to when lining up edges, and the spot where both sites are visible from under the tunnel.

callouts.name: Mid Pallet
callouts.description: A spot near a corner of boxes in mid, which can be scanned from Mid Blue.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The spawn on the attacker side, with a ramp corner and a yellow crate near it that double as aim references. Its barriers drop at round start.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defenders' spawn, which sits close to a corner of B Hut.

Lotus.name: Lotus
Lotus.summary: Lotus has three sites (A, B and C) linked by rotating doors on the A and C sides, plus a breakable wall between A Main and A Link that opens a shortcut toward B Site. Movement tools include a quiet drop from A Top and rope ascenders, so attackers often split routes while defenders rotate through the spawn area.

A Site: Attackers: clear A Main with utility before pushing, since the breakable wall to A Link gives a second entry and defenders can break it to flank.
Attackers: smoke the stairs and A Cubby first, then push A Tree with two players and send the rest in once the tree is secured.
Defenders: hold A Tree and check A Drop for flanks from A Top. If the A Link wall breaks, expect pressure coming through A Main.
B Site: Attackers: push B Main and B Upper together and watch A Link and C Link, since rotations from either side reach B quickly.
Attackers: smoke the back of B so defenders cannot hold B Default Box, then post-plant behind the central pillar.
Defenders: hold near the central pillar for cover, delay with utility on B Main, and call rotations early because B is hard to retake once attackers get crossfires.
C Site: Attackers: smoke Waterfall and C Link to block the elevated defender spot, then use the C Mound door for a split while the rest enter C Main.
Attackers: watch C Lobby before entering C Main, since defenders there can hit you when the C door is active.
Defenders: a single player in C can gather info and fall back for a retake. Rotate through the defender spawn rather than the loud C door.

callouts.name: A Door
callouts.description: The rotating door between A Main and A Rubble. Attackers use it as a quick shortcut onto A Site, and defenders can push through it to surprise attackers in A Rubble.

callouts.name: A Drop
callouts.description: A drop reached from A Top that lands inside A Site.

callouts.name: A Hut
callouts.description: A wall structure inside A Site that, together with the surrounding walls, forms a small maze.

callouts.name: A Link
callouts.description: A Link is on the A side and is reached from A Main through the breakable wall.

callouts.name: A Lobby
callouts.description: An attacker-side area on the approach to A, one of the lanes attackers can take at round start.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.description: The long-range duel lane leading onto A Site. Most A fights happen here, and the breakable wall to A Link sits along it.

callouts.name: A Root
callouts.description: Part of the A Root and A Rubble round-start lane. Defenders who push through A Door can catch attackers standing here by surprise.

callouts.name: A Rubble
callouts.description: The area reached through A Door from A Main.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The A plant area, enclosed by the walls around A Hut. It is called out to mark the spike or enemies that have moved inside.

callouts.name: A Stairs
callouts.description: A risky push route into A Site that can flank toward A Top.

callouts.name: A Top
callouts.description: A high flank point reached from A Stairs, and the spot where players walk silently to A Drop.

callouts.name: A Tree
callouts.description: An entry route into A Site reached through a swinging door. Defenders often hold near it at the back of the site, so it is called out for holds and entries.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.description: A narrow corridor leading into B Site that both teams use as the direct path.

callouts.name: B Pillars
callouts.description: One of the round-start lanes that leads toward B Site past the pillars.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: A compact site with a central pillar that gives cover, and defenders gain an advantage from its high ground.

callouts.name: B Upper
callouts.description: Players use it for splits and to warn of a flank from above.

callouts.name: C Bend
callouts.description: A bend on the route into C Site.

callouts.name: C Door
callouts.description: The rotating door on the C side that connects to C Main and C Mound.

callouts.name: C Elbow
callouts.description: The bend at the bottom of C Site where C Main turns onto the site, a close angle on anyone walking in.

callouts.name: C Gravel
callouts.description: The gravel path on the defender side of C, between C Hall and C Link, used to rotate between C and B.

callouts.name: C Hall
callouts.description: A passage on the defender side of C Site, part of its multi-level layout.

callouts.name: C Link
callouts.description: A defender-side passage on C Site that connects toward the other sites.

callouts.name: C Lobby
callouts.description: One of the round-start lanes for attackers. Attackers here can hit defenders who take C Main while the C door is active.

callouts.name: C Main
callouts.description: The attackers' main route into C Site. Defenders who hold it can be hit from C Lobby and B Main when the rotating door opens.

callouts.name: C Mound
callouts.description: A C-side area reached through a rotating door from C Main. Players use it for flanks and splits.

callouts.name: C Site
callouts.description: A larger, multi-level maze holding C Waterfall, C Hall and C Link.

callouts.name: C Waterfall
callouts.description: An elevated defender position on C Site near C Platform. Defenders hold it to control the site.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The attackers' starting area, where the three round-start lanes to A, B and C begin.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defenders' starting area, used as a safer rotation route between sites and as the retake approach.

Pearl.name: Pearl
Pearl.summary: Pearl is a two-site map where nearly every attacker and defender route runs through Mid, so controlling the central plaza decides most rotations. The A side is a cluster of tight corners with Art, Main and Dugout as the main entries, while B is wider, with a ramp-and-main approach and an elevated Tower that overlooks the site. Defenders leave from a spawn area fed by a water route that reaches both Mid and the sites.

A Site: Smoke the Secret and Flowers opening from Mid Plaza before the push, since most flank peeks come through that window.
Clear Dugout early and in the same push as A Main so the hard corner is not left for a late defender to hold.
Lurk or Sage-wall Art from Mid Top before committing, because Art has a single entrance and one player there can cut off the flank.
B Site: Expect a defender camp in the B Main and B Ramp corner, and clear it with a grenade before stepping into the open.
Use B Tunnel as a split when you only have one smoke, so you are not forced to spend both smokes on B Main.
Smoke B Tower and clear B Hall before planting, and keep an eye on B Link since it is the defenders' safest retake route.
Mid: Get an early presence on Mid Plaza, because whoever holds it controls the rotation paths to both sites.
Take Mid Top early, since it is the only way into Art and blocking it stops the flank before it starts.
Use Mid Connector and Mid Doors as wall-smoke origins to cut sightlines onto B Screen and A Main from a distance.

callouts.name: A Art
callouts.description: A walled-in gallery area between Mid Plaza and A Link whose only entrance from mid is through Mid Top, so players call it when the attackers are taking the flank toward A.

callouts.name: A Dugout
callouts.description: A corner inside A Site beside the boxes that is hard to clear in a straight duel, which is why attackers usually clear it early with A Main.

callouts.name: A Flowers
callouts.description: An A Site zone on the far side of the Secret opening, separated from it by a window, and a common target for wall smokes from mid.

callouts.name: A Link
callouts.description: The stair-up entry on A that opens into the site once Art is cleared, so its top is a standard smoke target when pushing.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.description: The main entrance onto A Site, which attackers move through with a push and defenders watch for flanks, and which is often walled off from Mid Doors.

callouts.name: A Restaurant
callouts.description: An area close to A Site and A Main that attackers use as a staging point before committing to the site.

callouts.name: A Secret
callouts.description: An opening inside A Site beside A Tower and A Flowers, and the wall target most often used from Mid Plaza to block the junction shared with A Link.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The A bomb site itself, the area where the spike is planted, entered from A Main and A Link.

callouts.name: B Club
callouts.description: The club building on the attacker side of B, between attacker spawn and B Ramp, where B pushes are set up.

callouts.name: B Cubby
callouts.description: A small nook along B Main where a defender can wait for attackers pushing through the lane.

callouts.name: B Hall
callouts.description: A corridor on the B side between B Tower, B Link and the site that holds a cubby, which defenders use for angles on B Link and the long plant spot.

callouts.name: B Link
callouts.description: A passage on B that sits beside B Main and B Hall, and is the safer retake entry for defenders because a player in B Main can cover it.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.description: The wide main entrance to B Site, which needs two smokes for a full execute and is the approach most attackers take first.

callouts.name: B Ramp
callouts.description: The ramp onto B Site on the opposite side from B Main, where a corner between the two is a common camping spot for defenders.

callouts.name: B Screen
callouts.description: The cover area inside B Site, a pocket behind a screen where spikes get planted and defenders reposition, which is covered by a wall from Mid Connector along with B Tower and B Hall.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The B bomb site, reached through B Main or B Ramp and bordered by B Hall, B Tower and the screen pocket.

callouts.name: B Tower
callouts.description: An elevated position over the B side with a single climb-up access point and long sightlines, from which defenders hold the site and attackers smoke and flash it clear.

callouts.name: B Tunnel
callouts.description: A split route into B Site that attackers use when they have only one smoke, giving an alternative to pushing through B Main.

callouts.name: Mid Connector
callouts.description: A passage in mid linking the mid doors, A Link and the defender-side water, which supports rotations between the sites and is the origin of the wall smoke toward B Screen.

callouts.name: Mid Doors
callouts.description: The door entrance on the mid side that A Main and A Link can be walled off from, making it the common setup point for blocking the A entry.

callouts.name: Mid Market
callouts.description: The market area at the attacker end of mid, between Mid Top and A Restaurant.

callouts.name: Mid Plaza
callouts.description: The central hub of mid that opens rotation paths to both sites, and the spot where players place early smokes to deny attacker sightlines onto A Secret and A Flowers.

callouts.name: Mid Shops
callouts.description: A group of mid spaces where defenders throw an early smoke to deny attackers vision of the central lanes.

callouts.name: Mid Top
callouts.description: The upper mid entrance and the only way into A Art, so players use it to flag enemies pushing from the attacker side toward the flank.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The attackers' starting room, the point every early rotation toward Mid and both sites begins from.

callouts.name: Defender Side Records
callouts.description: A spot on the defender side with two boxes nearby that players stand at when lobbing a molly onto B Site.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defenders' starting area, which a Killjoy turret can cover to spot approaches and which lurkers use to get information and flank.

callouts.name: Defender Side Water
callouts.description: The water route between Defender Spawn and Mid that also gives access toward both sites, so attackers can rotate through it for a surprise push onto B.

Abyss.name: Abyss
Abyss.summary: Abyss is a three-lane map where a huge void splits the middle, with the A and B sites at opposite ends. Mid acts as the connector: Mid Library and Mid Bottom feed the B side, while the vent, the ascenders and the Catwalk give vertical routes up to A's high ground. The open map edges mean a bad jump can drop a player off the map, so movement matters as much as utility.

A Site: Clear Sentinel utility such as trapwires and nanobots before the team pushes through A Main, because the entry is wide enough for the whole team to go together.
Split the attack so that a pair enters through A Vent while a trio holds A Main, which forces defenders to cover two entry lanes.
On defence, hold the high ground with a sniper who keeps moving, and stack utility in the narrow A entries so flankers coming through mid are caught early.
B Site: Use B Danger for a fast close entry, with teammates taking B Main after recon or flashes reveal the defenders, but remember that a misstep on the ledge drops you off the map.
As a defender, cover B Link and B Tower together, since both connect straight to the defender spawn and let attackers rotate quickly.
B is hard to hold alone, so pair a player on B Tower with a teammate below to cover the site from two heights.
Mid: Contest mid early as attackers, because controlling it gives access to both sites through Mid Library and Mid Bottom.
Post a player at Mid Library to watch the chokepoint for lurks and mid rushes, since it sees both the B link and the mid lane.
Treat Mid Catwalk and Mid Top as flank paths: they reach the A-side vent and the high ground, so holding them denies a route to A Tower.

callouts.name: A Bridge
callouts.description: A thin platform on the A side that players dash onto, and that also offers a plant option over the drop.

callouts.name: A Link
callouts.description: The passage running from mid to the A-side spawn, the back of A and the high ground above the site. It is a common line for rotations and for attackers moving toward A.

callouts.name: A Lobby
callouts.description: The route that starts at the attacker spawn and leads to A Main.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.description: The main approach into A Site from the attacker side. Defenders usually contest it early, and it is the choke that decides whether the A entry opens.

callouts.name: A Secret
callouts.description: A narrow ledge on the outer edge of the A side, reached by a hard jump across. It is a shortcut for players with strong movement, and a missed jump sends them off the map.

callouts.name: A Security
callouts.description: The spot tucked behind the large structure on A Site.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The A bombsite itself. Other A-side callouts, from A Tower above to A Vent and A Main below, are all named relative to it.

callouts.name: A Tower
callouts.description: The raised spot overlooking A Site, reached by the A ascender or by breaking the vent from mid. Holding it gives height over the site and makes retakes harder.

callouts.name: A Vent
callouts.description: A pair of breakable vent doors, each with 120 HP, linking A Site to mid. Once broken, the route stays open, and it is also the path toward A Tower from the Catwalk.

callouts.name: B Danger
callouts.description: A risky off-route on the far outer edge behind B Site, a narrow ledge where one misstep sends a player off the map. Attackers use it to reach B from behind the site.

callouts.name: B Link
callouts.description: The back route from Mid Library to B Site, and it also connects to B Tower and the defender spawn.

callouts.name: B Lobby
callouts.description: The attacker-side area that feeds B Main, where B pushes are set up.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.description: The main entrance into B Site, and the most direct lane for both teams. Attackers reach it from Mid Bottom.

callouts.name: B Nest
callouts.description: A holding spot near B Main from which a player watches angles into B Site.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The B bombsite. B Main, B Link, B Tower and B Danger all either lead into it or overlook it.

callouts.name: B Tower
callouts.description: A raised position above B Site, reached through the back-area link. It gives height on the site and connects to the defender spawn.

callouts.name: Mid Bend
callouts.description: A ledge area on the mid side that is reached by a rope ascender from B Main. It links the B lane directly to the middle of the map.

callouts.name: Mid Bottom
callouts.description: The lower mid passage that connects the mid area to B Main. Attackers coming through mid use it to reach the B entrance.

callouts.name: Mid Catwalk
callouts.description: An elevated path across mid. Players reach it by jumping a gap from Mid Top or Mid Library and then using an ascender, and it leads to the vent toward A Tower.

callouts.name: Mid Library
callouts.description: The rear-central area that links mid to B Site from behind. It is a chokepoint for lurks and mid rushes.

callouts.name: Mid Top
callouts.description: The upper part of mid near Mid Library, and the jump-off point for reaching Mid Catwalk.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The attacker starting area, where the A Lobby route begins. One of the map's three ascenders sits in this spawn zone.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defender starting area. B Link and B Tower both lead out from here toward the back of B and mid.

Corrode.name: Corrode
Corrode.summary: Corrode is a three-lane, two-site map set in a fortified castle town, with a lot of verticality, many thin walls, and tight off-angles. The mid lane links both bombsites through a staircase section and a window overlooking the lane, so controlling it gives teams split options. Each site has a main entrance, a fallback area, and elevated positions that reward careful utility use.

A Site: Take Yard before planting. It is the open area attackers reach after A Main or A Link, and splitting pressure through Link and Main is a common way to get there.
Clearing Pocket and Elbow gives attackers a fallback position to hold after the plant.
As defenders, contest A Link early. Holding Elbow keeps some control of the site when the attackers push ground.
B Site: Take Mid before committing to B, then combine a Main push with a pivot from Mid through B Link.
B Elbow is one of the few fallback spots on B, so the team that wins it usually controls the post-plant hold.
As defenders, B Tower is the way back in after losing the site. The narrow entries and elevated angles also favor a holding defense.
Mid: Contest Mid early. Control of the lane opens split options to both sites, so it is the main priority for either side.
Attackers often start with a 1-3-1 setup, clear Mid Bottom first, then push through Mid Stairs toward Mid Top.
Mid Stairs gives a quick pivot into A and Mid Top gives one into B. Defenders should keep one player on the fast mid rotate and watch the lane's extremities.

callouts.name: A Box
callouts.description: The boxes on A Site by the plant area, cover for a planter and for a defender holding the site.

callouts.name: A Crane
callouts.description: An A-side entrance that defenders commonly use, reached through the defender-side route, so players call it when a fight starts at that door into A.

callouts.name: A Elbow
callouts.description: A bend on the A-side approach near Yard and Pocket that both teams fight over, since holding it keeps a fallback spot on the site.

callouts.name: A Link
callouts.description: The corridor connecting A to Mid. Both sides contest it, and control of it often decides whether A can be taken or held.

callouts.name: A Lobby
callouts.description: The outer area that leads toward A from the attacker side.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.description: The main attacker entrance into A. Early pushes here are often less valuable because defenders can fall back, so players call it when someone takes that entrance.

callouts.name: A Pocket
callouts.description: A nook on the A side, next to Elbow, that attackers clear on the safer route into A.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The A bombsite area itself, covering the planting zone and the positions around it, so players use it for the whole site.

callouts.name: A Yard
callouts.description: The open area attackers reach after passing A Main or A Link. Teams usually want to control it before planting, and it is a common flash point.

callouts.name: B Arch
callouts.description: An entrance into B on the defender-side route, comparable to A Crane on the A side.

callouts.name: B Elbow
callouts.description: A bend on the B approach that both teams want to hold. It is one of the few fallback spots on B, so players call it when deciding a post-plant hold.

callouts.name: B Link
callouts.description: The connecting route from Mid into B and a common pivot point.

callouts.name: B Lobby
callouts.description: The outer area on the B side whose edges matter for flanks during a round, similar in role to A Lobby.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.description: The main entrance into B and the usual front-door attacker push.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The B bombsite area itself. It is compact and tends to be held from elevated angles.

callouts.name: B Tower
callouts.description: An elevated position overlooking B. Defenders can use it to re-enter the site after losing control, so players call it when it is taken or smoked.

callouts.name: Mid Bottom
callouts.description: The lower section of Mid nearest the attacker side, which attackers often take first before pushing further into the lane.

callouts.name: Mid Stairs
callouts.description: A staircase in the mid lane between Mid Bottom and Mid Top. Control there gives attackers a quick pivot into A.

callouts.name: Mid Top
callouts.description: The upper section of Mid, between Mid Stairs and Mid Window. Control there gives a quick pivot toward B.

callouts.name: Mid Window
callouts.description: A window spot overlooking the mid lane, next to Mid Top.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The attackers' starting area. Players reference it as the origin of the route out toward A through the A Lobby.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defenders' starting area and the origin of their rotations. It is also a route for mid-round pivots toward A Crane.

Breeze.name: Breeze
Breeze.summary: Breeze is a tropical map with two spike sites, A and B, joined by a central Mid that offers routes into both, and its long sightlines reward careful angle control.

A Site: After the 12.00 rework the A Hall door is fenced: you can see and shoot through it but nothing crosses, so don't spend a player guarding it from the cave side.
A Shop is now the only way into A Cave, so a player posted near the Shop catches pushes early and turns the cave into a dead end for attackers.
Cover the rope routes: the back-site rope and the A Lobby rope both climb to Bridge, so a teammate on Bridge or near the rope shuts down flanks.
B Site: Use B Main and B Tunnel together: attackers can enter from both, so put one defender on the Tunnel angle while the main player watches the wider B Main approach.
Don't count on jumping the Elbow wall; the rework raised it, so route enemies through B Main or Tunnel instead.
B Back is a trap spot for attackers, so don't dump into it without a flash; defenders can hold it with Viper or Killjoy setups behind the brick tower.
Mid: With one entrance to Mid after 12.00, a player on the Mid Cubby can ambush anyone who peeks the boxes, so use the cubby rather than peeking the open center.
Clear Mid Nest before a B retake, since it sees both sites and a sniper there can punish a rotating team.

callouts.name: A Bridge
callouts.description: Bridge is reached by the rope at the back of A Site and leads onward into A Hall, so a call here means someone is crossing toward the hall or coming up that rope.

callouts.name: A Hall
callouts.description: The halls between Mid and A Site, the route for attackers who take mid and swing onto A.

callouts.name: A Lobby
callouts.description: A Lobby holds the attacker-side rope that climbs up to Bridge and then into A Hall, so calls for it warn that enemies are using that climb.

callouts.name: A Pyramids
callouts.description: A Pyramids are the raised cover structures on A Site that attackers plant in front of and that offer long angles, so players call them out when someone holds them over the plant zone.

callouts.name: A Ramp
callouts.description: The ramp below A Bridge on the defender side of A, the route between A and the top of mid.

callouts.name: A Rope
callouts.description: The rope by A Shop that climbs up toward the halls, a quick vertical route on the A side.

callouts.name: A Shop
callouts.description: A Shop is the room on the A side that works as the gate into A Cave, and since the 12.00 rework it is the only way into that cave, so calls for it warn that enemies are pushing through the Shop.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: A Site is the spike site on the A side, reached from A Main, A Cave and the Mid door, and its callouts mark where defenders hold and where attackers plant.

callouts.name: A Yellow
callouts.description: The yellow container between A Bridge and A Site, cover on the defender side of the site.

callouts.name: B Back
callouts.description: B Back is the space behind the brick tower at the far end of the B Site wall, a common Viper or Killjoy setup, so players call it out when someone is hiding there or an attacker gets trapped in the back site.

callouts.name: B Elbow
callouts.description: B Elbow is the bent passage that links Mid Top to B Site and is used for flanks and rotations; the rework raised its wall so it can no longer be jumped, so a call here means someone is coming around that bend.

callouts.name: B Ladder
callouts.description: The ladder at the back of B Site, a climb defenders use to hold the site from an off angle.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.description: B Main is the wider of the two attacker entrances into B Site and the first contact point for many B executes, so calling it means someone is holding or pushing the approach.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: B Site is the spike site on the B side, entered from B Main and B Tunnel, and since the 12.00 rework a wall splits it in two, so calls often specify which half an enemy is in.

callouts.name: B Tunnel
callouts.description: B Tunnel is the second attacker entrance into B Site beside B Main, and holders there get sniper angles, so the call warns that an enemy has taken the tunnel side.

callouts.name: B Wall
callouts.description: B Wall is the wall on B Site that attackers can take control of from Top Mid and that defenders can play aggressively from, so calls for it mean someone is peeking off that wall.

callouts.name: B Window
callouts.description: B Window is the opening on the back side of B Site, and players call it out when an enemy is watching the site through it.

callouts.name: Mid Bottom
callouts.description: The attacker end of mid, where attackers come in from spawn before taking mid.

callouts.name: Mid Cannon
callouts.description: The cannon on the B side of mid, the open stretch attackers cross from mid toward B Elbow.

callouts.name: Mid Hall
callouts.description: The hall between mid and A beside Mid Wood Doors, the defenders' rotation route from mid to A.

callouts.name: Mid Nest
callouts.description: Mid Nest is the elevated sniper position in Mid that watches Mid Doors and mid pushes, and it must be cleared in B retakes, so calls for it report a sniper threatening both sites.

callouts.name: Mid Pillar
callouts.description: Mid Pillar is the central pillar that splits Mid, and after the rework a wall beside it was extended so Mid has one entrance, so calls for it mark fights at the center of Mid.

callouts.name: Mid Top
callouts.description: Mid Top is the top-side route through Mid that attackers use to hit B Site, pairing with B Main and connecting to B Elbow, so calling it out tracks enemies heading toward B from Mid.

callouts.name: Mid Wood Doors
callouts.description: Mid Wood Doors are the doors on the Mid side that open onto A Site, and teams push through them, so calls for these doors warn of an A-site push from Mid.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The attacker spawn is where the attacking team starts each round, and calls from it usually report enemies moving out early along the attacking routes.

callouts.name: Defender Side Arches
callouts.description: Arches is the defender-side archway on the front of B Site near B Wall, and calls there mark defenders holding the arch or attackers pushing toward it.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defender spawn is where defenders start and the main route for rotating between the two spike sites, so calls from it track early defender movement.

Summit.name: Summit
Summit.summary: Summit is a two-site, three-lane 5v5 map set in a Radiant training academy, with Mid acting as the central hub that links both bombsites through Mid Fountain. Three droppable walls, one each at A Site, Mid and B Site, are triggered by shooting nearby switches and then stay closed for the rest of the round, so rotations can change partway through a round. A Site is the smaller bombsite and needs more defensive calls, while B Site is larger and has elevated defender positions.

A Site: Clear Garden and the close angles before committing to a push, since the site is small and fights happen fast.
Use utility on the CT Boxes angle before going in, because defenders tend to hold those spots tightly.
When defending, remember the A Wall can cut off the escape route you were counting on once it drops.
B Site: Clear Close Box and the deeper B-side angles before planting, since they can punish a plant.
Watch for a silent flank from B Drop and B Tower when you are on the B side.
Time the B Wall drop around executes so defenders cannot rotate through that route.
Mid: Take Mid Fountain before committing to a site, because it lets you rotate to either side.
Keep at least one player watching Mid each round so attackers cannot easily split pressure.
Use Mid Window for lurks and information plays rather than standing in the open.

callouts.name: A Art
callouts.description: The art room on the defender side of A, between A Hall and A Cave, a hold and rotation spot behind the site.

callouts.name: A Cave
callouts.description: A side pocket that a push coming down A Main can branch into, alongside the routes toward A Garden and A Site.

callouts.name: A Garden
callouts.description: An open, close-angle stretch on the approach to A Site, reached from A Main, that teams usually clear before planting.

callouts.name: A Hall
callouts.description: The hallway on the defender side of A that links mid to A Art.

callouts.name: A Link
callouts.description: The connector between Mid and A Site, reached through Mid Bend or Mid Fountain, giving a quick second route from Mid onto A.

callouts.name: A Lobby
callouts.description: An attacker-side area fed directly from the attacker spawn that gives access to A Site.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.description: The main attacking route toward A Site, which branches into A Garden and A Cave.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.description: The smaller of the two bombsites; holding it takes more defensive calls than holding B Site.

callouts.name: B Drop
callouts.description: The drop at the far back of B Site, a one-way way down onto the site.

callouts.name: B Gym
callouts.description: The gym on the defender side of B behind B Tower, the rotation route from defender spawn to B.

callouts.name: B Link
callouts.description: The connector from Mid Bottom to B Site, and the main B-side route out of Mid.

callouts.name: B Lobby
callouts.description: An attacker-side area fed by the attacker spawn that gives access to B Site.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.description: The main attacking route toward B Site.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.description: The larger bombsite, with simpler callouts than A Site and a defender-side droppable wall that changes how it plays.

callouts.name: B Tower
callouts.description: The raised tower at the back of B Site, a high angle over the plant and the B Main entrance.

callouts.name: B Trophy
callouts.description: A deeper B-side defensive area that holds up for retakes; teams smoke or clear it before settling post-plant.

callouts.name: Mid Bend
callouts.description: A passage leading from Mid toward A Link, reached from the Mid Fountain area.

callouts.name: Mid Bottom
callouts.description: The lower Mid section that feeds B Link and Mid Window, important for B splits and retakes.

callouts.name: Mid Fountain
callouts.description: The central junction in Mid where routes split toward either site.

callouts.name: Mid Tiles
callouts.description: The tiled walkway between mid and B Lobby, a rotation path from mid toward B.

callouts.name: Mid Top
callouts.description: The upper Mid section that feeds Mid Tiles, Mid Fountain, Mid Bend and Mid Bottom, and that attackers enter Mid through.

callouts.name: Mid Window
callouts.description: An opening off Mid Bottom used for lurks and information plays on the B side of Mid.

callouts.name: Attacker Side Spawn
callouts.description: The attacker spawn, which feeds straight into both A Lobby and B Lobby.

callouts.name: Defender Side Spawn
callouts.description: The defender spawn at the bottom center of the map, connecting to both sites.
